If it needs two workers or threads to interleave at a particular point, say whether the code as written lets them interleave there: separate heaps except explicitly shared memory, and no Atomics ordering that rules the interleaving out. subclaims.reason: lib/priority-queue.js:100 calls _this.queues.reverse() at the top of every loop pass, and Array#reverse reverses in place, so successive passes alternate between [critical..low] and [low..critical] (initial order low..critical is set at lib/priority-queue.js:24-27). Every second pass therefore visits low first. The loop is a single sequential Promise.each chain re-entered via .then(loop) (lib/priority-queue.js:100-125), reached by any caller of process() (lib/priority-queue.js:84-91); no workers, threads, or second-callback interleave is needed.
caveats: Relies on standard JS semantics: Array.prototype.reverse sorts in place and returns the same array.
Assumes the normal single run loop from process(); resume() can start a second loop sharing this.queues (lib/priority-queue.js:157-167).

subclaims.reason: On the reversed (critical-first, 1st/odd) pass, critical sits at index 0, so lib/priority-queue.js:101 assigns it Strategy.exponential(0) = Math.pow(0,0)*2 = 2 (lib/priority-queue.js:229-231), the minimum budget on that pass (tied with index 1; index 4 gets 512). Critical thus gets the smallest per-pass job budget on odd passes. Same single-sequential-loop path as B5.1 (lib/priority-queue.js:94-129); no interleaving across workers, threads, or loop callbacks is needed.
caveats: Relies on standard JS semantics: Math.pow(0,0) === 1, so Strategy.exponential(0) is 2.
Budgets follow the per-pass index, so they alternate along with the pass order; same single-loop assumption as B5.1.
